messages.content: Find a board game with complexity rating under 2.5 and that supports more than 5 players, as well as a trivia game that could be played within 60 minutes.

function.name: card_game_search
function.description: Locate a card game based on a specific theme. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

theme.description: The theme for the card game.

function.name: board_game_search
function.description: Locate a board game based on specific criteria. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

complexity.description: The maximum complexity rating of the board game (lower is simpler). This is a float type value.

player_count.description: The minimum player count for the board game.

function.name: trivia_game_search
function.description: Locate a trivia game based on play duration. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

duration.description: The maximum playing duration for the trivia game in minutes. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
We need to call two functions:

1) board_game_search with complexity < 2.5 and player_count > 5.

But note the parameter names: "complexity" expects max complexity; we want less than 2.5 so pass 2.5? Actually it's "maximum complexity rating". So if we set complexity=2.5 it will return games <=2.5. Good.

Also "minimum player count": we want support more than 5 players. That means min player count >=6. But param says "the minimum player count for the board game." If we set player_count=6 then results should have at least 6 players. Good.

So call board_game_search({complexity: 2.5, player_count: 6})

2) trivia_game_search with duration <=60. Parameter name "duration" is maximum playing duration. So pass 60.

Call trivia_game_search({duration: 60})

We'll produce calls accordingly.
